Lucid Trading.long:
Lucid Trading is a futures funded-account provider. Its substantive difference from most competitors is the drawdown mechanic: the trailing loss floor is recalculated at the end of the session rather than continuously, so an unrealised spike during the day does not permanently raise the floor the way an intraday trailing model does. That distinction is the one worth understanding, because it changes what a given maximum-loss figure actually means in practice.

As advertised through 2026, the firm runs several paths: a conventional evaluation, an instant-funding option carrying a tighter consistency requirement, and a variant with no daily loss limit and no funded-stage consistency rule. Account sizes run from roughly 25,000 to 150,000, with one-off evaluation fees rather than monthly charges, profit splits at the higher end of the sector, and unusually fast payout processing. The firm reported passing 100 million dollars in cumulative payouts in March 2026.

The standard caveats apply and are not diminished by any of the above. Funded accounts here are simulated futures accounts, as they are almost everywhere in this sector, so the counterparty is the firm and not an exchange. Public complaints follow the sector pattern too: verification delays, and disputes over whether a rule was breached.

Where people get fooled: reading a favourable comparison as independent. Essentially all available material on this firm and its competitors is published by affiliate sites paid per referral, and the figures above will age — LucidFlex only launched in late 2025, and firms in this sector rewrite terms without much notice. The rulebook on the firm's own site at the moment of purchase is the only version that binds anyone.
Lucid Trading.usage: Named as the common example of a futures programme using end-of-day rather than intraday trailing drawdown.
